description:
The oil seller’s hometown reaches the opening through a pie recipe and remembered food, not a world-map exposition scene. Its architecture, residents and wider role remain undeveloped; it is not established as either Koga settlement.

Proposed future recognition: a baker folds pastry scraps into a smaller pie rather than throwing them away. The seller’s recipe can be recognized by its folded edge before somebody tells the player where they are. A local may disagree about how much butter belongs in it; home memories need not be geographically exact. These details give the place a familiar taste and craft without fixing its location, population or wider quest.

links.description: Bible proposal: extend the plate’s blue-reed motif into the hometown’s household pottery. The child could notice reeds painted unevenly on bowls in ordinary kitchens, not an emblem reserved for a sacred order or magical heraldry.

Sections 5–6: places and characters; working names versus identities

§5.12: hometown, recipe and possible pottery recognition. Pastry-making and recipe disagreement are new proposals.
